install.use_pnpm: {{workingDirectory}} was installed with npm. pnpm is faster and runs no dependency install scripts unless you allow them: install it (npm install -g pnpm), run "pnpm import" to convert package-lock.json, delete package-lock.json and run "pnpm add -D @dcl/sdk-commands@{{version}}" so the scripts find the CLI.

build.js_runtime_version: @dcl/js-runtime {{runtime}} is installed next to @dcl/sdk {{sdk}}. Each pins its own @dcl/ecs, so the ~system module types can disagree with the scene's: install @dcl/js-runtime@{{sdk}}.

bundle.tsconfig_base_url_removed: TypeScript 7 removed the "baseUrl" option: it was deleted from {{tsconfig}} and the "paths" entries were made relative to that file. Keep this change.
bundle.tsconfig_star_path_added: {{tsconfig}} now maps "*" to "{{target}}" under "paths", so imports that resolved through "baseUrl" keep working; delete that entry if the scene has no such imports.
bundle.tsconfig_strict_default_kept: TypeScript 7 turns "strict" on by default: {{tsconfig}} now sets "strict": false, the setting this scene was type-checked with so far. Switch it to true when the scene is ready for the strict checks.
bundle.tsconfig_not_writable: {{tsconfig}} uses the "baseUrl" option, which TypeScript 7 removed, and could not be rewritten: {{error}}. Delete "baseUrl" and start each "paths" entry with ./
bundle.tsconfig_strict_unresolved: TypeScript 7 turns "strict" on by default and {{tsconfig}} does not set it. Whether a file it extends does is unknown, because "{{target}}" could not be resolved, so "strict" was left alone: set it in {{tsconfig}} to choose the checks the scene builds with.
bundle.tsconfig_strict_not_writable: {{tsconfig}} does not set "strict", which TypeScript 7 turns on by default, and could not be rewritten: {{error}}. Set "strict": false in it to keep the checks the scene was type-checked with so far, or true to adopt the strict checks.
